defmodule AuthService.TokenValidator do
  @moduledoc """
  Validates authentication tokens with multi-layer security checks.
  Supports internationalized usernames per RFC 8264 (PRECIS framework).
  """

  @max_username_length 64
  @max_token_length 512
  @allowed_schemes ["bearer", "basic", "digest"]

  # Pattern validates: scheme + space + base64url token segments separated by dots
  # Uses atomic grouping equivalent via split-then-validate approach
  @token_format_pattern ~r/\A(bearer|basic|digest)\s+(.+)\z/i

  # Username pattern: allows word chars, dots, hyphens only
  # Applied AFTER normalization and length re-check
  @username_pattern ~r/\A[a-z0-9._\-]{1,64}\z/

  defstruct [:username, :token_scheme, :token_body, :validated_at]

  @doc "Validates a full auth header value with username context"
  def validate_auth(username, auth_header) when is_binary(username) and is_binary(auth_header) do
    with {:ok, normalized_user} <- validate_and_normalize_username(username),
         {:ok, scheme, token_body} <- parse_auth_header(auth_header),
         :ok <- verify_token_integrity(token_body) do
      {:ok, %__MODULE__{
        username: normalized_user,
        token_scheme: scheme,
        token_body: token_body,
        validated_at: System.system_time(:second)
      }}
    end
  end
  def validate_auth(_, _), do: {:error, :invalid_input}

  @doc "Normalize username per PRECIS UsernameCaseMapped profile"
  defp validate_and_normalize_username(username) do
    # Step 1: Length check on raw input (prevents obvious abuse)
    if byte_size(username) > @max_username_length do
      {:error, :username_too_long}
    else
      # Step 2: Apply NFKD normalization (as per PRECIS framework)
      normalized = :unicode.characters_to_nfkd_binary(username)
      
      # Step 3: Case fold for case-insensitive comparison
      folded = String.downcase(normalized)
      
      # Step 4: Re-check length AFTER normalization (NFKD can expand)
      if byte_size(folded) > @max_username_length do
        {:error, :username_too_long_after_normalization}
      else
        # Step 5: Validate against strict ASCII character pattern
        if Regex.match?(@username_pattern, folded) do
          {:ok, folded}
        else
          {:error, :invalid_username_chars}
        end
      end
    end
  end

  defp parse_auth_header(header) do
    # Length check before any processing
    if byte_size(header) > @max_token_length do
      {:error, :token_too_long}
    else
      case Regex.run(@token_format_pattern, header) do
        [_full, scheme, body] ->
          # Validate token body structure without backtracking-prone regex
          if valid_token_structure?(body) do
            {:ok, String.downcase(scheme), body}
          else
            {:error, :invalid_auth_format}
          end
        _ ->
          {:error, :invalid_auth_format}
      end
    end
  end

  defp valid_token_structure?(body) do
    # Split on dots and validate each segment is base64-like
    segments = String.split(body, ".")
    length(segments) >= 1 and length(segments) <= 5 and
      Enum.all?(segments, fn seg ->
        byte_size(seg) > 0 and byte_size(seg) <= 512 and
          Regex.match?(~r/\A[A-Za-z0-9+\/]+=*\z/, seg)
      end)
  end

  defp verify_token_integrity(token_body) do
    # Verify it's valid base64 (with dots as segment separators)
    segments = String.split(token_body, ".")
    
    if Enum.all?(segments, &valid_base64_segment?/1) do
      :ok
    else
      {:error, :invalid_token_encoding}
    end
  end

  defp valid_base64_segment?(segment) do
    case Base.decode64(segment, padding: false) do
      {:ok, _} -> true
      :error ->
        case Base.decode64(segment) do
          {:ok, _} -> true
          :error -> false
        end
    end
  end
end
